There was once a mysterious island called Isola,\n
home to a tribe of lost refugees.\n
One day a child made a discovery.\n
on a forbidden path, at the edge of the village.\n
The elders gathered to examine the mask.\n
They had never seen one like it before.\n
They must determine if others are nearby, so they appoint\n
a small group of villagers to search the forbidden path.\n
The path took them into the darkest parts of the jungle.\n
Although they could see no one, they sensed they were being watched.\n
Your villagers have been captured and are now the prisoners of this faceless tribe!\n
Do you need help getting started?\n
On this day the new believer told his sad story.\n
Long ago there was a war between two factions in the island.\n
The conflict began with a forbidden love...\n
but ended with bloodshed and destruction.\n
Those who survived the battle fled into the night.\n
We retreated into the jungle and into a despair\n
so deep and suffocating that we lost all hope.\n
We stopped believing in the island, in any guiding force.\n
We stopped even believing in ourselves, and so we covered\n
our faces with hideous masks. We were truly lost.\n
Your kindness, your words and actions, have helped me to see the truth.\n
The others must also be rescued from their eternal prison of hopelessness,\n
as I have been. We must help the others to believe again.\n
Our chief... he had a daughter...\n
I had forgotten that love. I had forgotten everything!\n
Seeing this necklace again has opened my eyes at last!\n
The chief's hope and faith have been restored.\n
The lost heathens have been found... the hopeless given hope.\n
The new believers have been set free,\n
and faith has been restored to Isola!\n

Let's explore the area...
 Click and hold the mouse button 
 anywhere on the ground and drag the 
 mouse to move around the village.

Good! This is how you move about 
 the island. Feel free to explore your
 little village.

Let's get to know one of the villagers...
 Find and click a villager, one without a mask, 
 to select them.

Perfect! A white circle shows which 
 villager is selected. See important 
 details about this villager, like their 
 name, at the bottom of the screen.

Let's move a villager...
 Click and hold the mouse button 
 on a villager and drag the mouse 
 to move them.

Excellent! Moving villagers influences their 
 behavior. Drag and drop villagers anywhere 
 you like to help them explore useful or 
 interesting places in the village.

Your villagers interact with many 
 locations around the map. Let's 
 start by dragging one of them to the green 
 bamboo fence that imprisons them.

Your villagers are using the green bamboo 
 to build a bin to store much-needed food. 
 Keep your villagers working on it.

You will notice there are villagers 
 wearing various colorful masks. 
 Find and click a villager wearing a blue mask.

You selected a heathen villager. 
 Heathen villagers don't believe in you, so 
 you cannot check their details or interfere with them. 
 Heathens wearing blue masks are not aggressive.
Find and click a villager wearing an orange mask.\n

You selected a heathen guard. 
 Heathens wearing orange masks are aggressive. 
 If they are approached by believers, they will chase them away.
Find and click a villager wearing a red mask.\n

You selected a senior heathen guard. 
 Heathens wearing red masks are scary. 
 They won't chase believers away, but they are 
 so scary that your villagers will run anyway.
Try dropping one of your villagers onto \n a heathen villager wearing a blue mask. \n

Good! Your villager is persuading 
 the heathen villager to believe in you. 
 When the heathen villager faith meter 
 crosses the middle, he or she will convert 
 and join your tribe of believers.

Villagers who believe in you increase your 
 Divine Energy. This unlocks God Powers. 
 Let's try a power now and spawn some butterflies. 
 Click the butterfly icon on the top left of the screen, 
 then click somewhere to release them.

Wow! Butterflies are great for distracting 
 children, both believers and heathens alike. 
 Notice how you used a little bit of your energy. 
 The more believers you have, the faster your 
 energy will replenish.

Let's teach one of your villagers to research...
 Drag an adult villager to the large 
 table at the center of the lab.

Oh no! Your villager is being chased away by the heathens! 
 The heathens occupy many areas of the village 
 and have erected totems as a symbol of their ownership. 
 In order to start research and gain tech points, you will need 
 to gain control of each area by dismantling the totems. 
 Once you take over the research area, your tribe can start 
 generating tech points.

Let's check out the Technologies screen...
 Click the 'Tech' button on the left side of 
 the screen.

Welcome to the Technologies screen. 
 Use the tech points gained from research 
 to upgrade a variety of different technologies. 
 The right side of the screen shows all the powers 
 you have unlocked, as well as those you have not yet unlocked. 
 They can be unlocked by increasing your divine energy. 
 Click 'Done' to return to the main screen.

Children can also contribute to village life. 
 Their keen eyes can spot mushrooms and small 
 collectibles that adults might overlook. 
 Drag a child to this collectible before it disappears.

Ooooh! The child found a relic! 
 Your villagers can collect Isola's small and 
 beautiful treasures, but only when found by 
 a child. Repeat relics are converted into 
 divine energy, while repeat lab gear gets converted into tech points.

Let's check out the Collections screen. 
 Click the 'Collections' button on the left 
 side of the screen.

Welcome to the Collections screen. 
 Here you can see which collectibles your 
 village children have gathered. Each relic that 
 you collect permanently increases your maximum 
 divine energy. Each piece of lab gear permanently 
 increases tech point production! 
 Click 'Done' to return to the main screen.

Let's learn more about a villager...
 Click the 'Detail' button at the 
 bottom of the screen.

Welcome to the Villager Detail screen. 
 Learn more about each villager, such 
 as faith, health and skills. Check the 
 box to the right of a skill to set a 
 skill preference. Click 'Done' to return 
 to the main screen.

You can see the status of the game's puzzles on the Puzzles and Milestones screen. 
 Click the 'Puzzles' button on the left 
 side of the screen.

Welcome to the Puzzles and Milestones screen. 
 The island is full of puzzles and hidden secrets 
 waiting to be discovered. Your goal is to solve 
 Isola's puzzles while helping your tribe 
 survive and make more new believers.

Well, as we approach the conclusion of this tutorial, 
 we arrive at the inevitable topic of making babies! 
 Deploy builders on the love shack to provide a romantic 
 place to get together. Take your time... When you manage 
 to get it finished, the final steps of the tutorial will resume.

Good!
 The love shack is a romantic hut and a perfect place 
 for village couples to discuss starting or adding to 
 their families and the tribe!

Let's make some babies...
 Drag an adult male villager onto an 
 adult female villager or vice versa. 
 A villager will not seek a mate on 
 their own unless they are trained and 
 Parenting is set as their preferred skill.

Good! They get along and want to 
 go indoors for some privacy. With any 
 luck, the stork may bring a new baby.

Welcome to Virtual Villagers: New Believers
 
 Oh no! Your villagers have been captured by a 
 faceless tribe of non-believers. They need to establish 
 themselves here in the center of Isola and try to help 
 these heathens regain some hope and faith.

Almost! Click and hold the mouse button 
 anywhere on the ground and drag the 
 mouse to move around the village.

Good! Let's wait while the villager gathers noni. 
 If they succeed, they will bring some to 
 the food bin near the center of the village.

Darn! The villager didn't succeed.
 Sometimes it takes a few tries, so drag 
 the same villager to the noni again.

Good! Let's give the villager a 
 moment to research. If they 
 succeed, you will earn tech points.

Oh, well! The villager was unsuccessful 
 at research. Drag the same villager to 
 the table again.

Too bad! They didn't get along or 
 aren't in the mood. Try again with 
 the same couple or try a different 
 pair to see if love blossoms.

Congratulations! The stork brought 
 a baby. Be careful! A mother 
 cares for her child until age two and 
 won't do much else.

Shoot! The villager is still sick. 
 Drag the same villager onto 
 the sick one again.

Hmmm... The villager is not convinced. 
 Drag the same villager onto 
 the heathen again.

How sad. One of your little villagers is dead. 
 Villagers die of old age, but they can also die 
 from disease and starvation. Buying medicine 
 technology helps your villagers live longer 
 and have fewer diseases.

Welcome to the Overview Map. 
 Enjoy a bird's-eye view of your village, 
 then click anywhere on the map to zoom 
 in to that spot.

Virtual Villagers is a true real-time game. 
 Your tribe continues to do what they have learned, 
 even when the computer is off or you stop playing, 
 but remember to check back often to care for 
 your little villagers! Have fun!

You have mastered the basics! 
 How you manage your tribe now is up to you! 
 Decide wisely who will do what. Your villagers 
 will slowly learn to do the tasks you show them. 
 Once survival is no longer an issue, you can 
 help them uncover the hidden secrets of Isola!

Hmmm... This villager is confused. 
 Sometimes villagers need more skill 
 or more advanced technology before 
 they understand what to do.

Great! You set a villager's skill preference. 
 From now on, they prefer this type of work 
 and gain skill the more they practice.

Nice try, but children don't work. They 
 love to play and won't do what you ask 
 until they grow up. They can still help 
 out though, as they sometimes find 
 delicious mushrooms or collectibles.
Nursing mothers don't work while they \n are caring for an infant. \n
Good. Let's watch this villager make a supply \n of cutting tools for the tribe. \n

Congratulations! One of your villagers 
 reached the `Trainee` level in a skill 
 category.

Congratulations! One of your villagers 
 reached the `Adept` level in a skill 
 category.

Good job! Your villagers aren't worried about 
 food anymore. Now you can focus on research 
 and increasing the population of the village.

One of the young children of your tribe is now 
 old enough to work! Your tribe needs every 
 able-bodied person to help out, so find that 
 villager, give them a job and keep everyone productive.
You cannot touch heathens because they do not believe in you.\n \n
You cannot view details about heathens. They do not believe in you.\n \n
You converted a heathen! Any time you make new believers, \n through conversion or new babies, you increase your max energy, \n which can eventually unlock new powers!
Some totems will require special powers to help your villagers \n remove them. If you are stuck, work on increasing population \n and collecting relics.
Recovering relics adds to your max energy, \n which can unlock new, exciting powers!
Assigning builders to polish the statue helps them to \n practice building and gives you a bit of energy each time!
You can only try to convert each heathen once, then you must wait a while before you can try again. \n The glowy light above them means they are tired of listening for now!
You have a new power! As you increase the number of \n people who believe in you, new powers become available.

One of your villagers is a master in a skill! 
 This is a great accomplishment. Making any one 
 villager a master in at least three skills grants 
 that villager the prestigious title of Elder.
Congratulations! Your village reached its \n first population milestone of 15 people!\n
Congratulations! Your village reached its \n second population milestone of 25 people!\n
Congratulations! Your village reached its \n third population milestone of 50 people!\n
Congratulations! Your village reached \n its maximum sustainable population!\n
Your villagers found an interesting new\n recipe!\n

Alas, the fates were not kind to your village. 
 There is nobody left who believes in you. The island 
 of Isola remains a myth and its mysteries 
 unsolved.

The Prison Break
 
 Your villagers have torn down the flimsy 
 bamboo fence and built a food bin from it. 
 Now they have a place to store food.

The Hungry Totem
 
 Your villagers have torn down an enemy totem. 
 Now they can add noni fruit to their diet.

The Blind Totem
 
 Your villagers have reactivated this peculiar totem. 
 Your vision in this area is restored!

The Rainbow Totem
 
 Your villagers have torn down an enemy totem. 
 The warm springs are now theirs to enjoy.

The Hollow Totem
 
 Your village children have broken an enemy totem. 
 The lake is now part of the believers' domain.

The Knowing Totem
 
 Your villagers have torn down an enemy totem. 
 They have gained access to the lab.

The Pain Totem
 
 Your villagers have torn down an enemy totem. 
 They have gained access to a healing area.

The Blocking Totem
 
 Your villagers have torn down an enemy totem. 
 They can now dig out the mausoleum safely.

The Sick Heathen
 
 Your villagers have cured a sick heathen, 
 who has now joined the believers!

The Heathen Chief
 
 Your villagers have finally convinced the 
 Heathen Chief to join their cause!

The Last Heathen
 
 Your villagers have finally convinced the 
 last of the heathen faction to join their cause!

The Tribute Statue
 
 Your villagers have sculpted a grand statue! 
 This will maximize accumulation of divine energy.

The Heathen Parent
 
 Your villagers have converted the heathen parent, 
 who has decided to join the believers!

The Nursery School
 
 Your villagers have built a nursery school. 
 This will help them raise smarter 
 children.

The Heathen Scientist
 
 Your villagers have convinced the heathen scientist 
 to join the believers!

The Heathen Builder
 
 Your villagers have convinced the heathen builder 
 to join the believers!

The Hydroponic Farm
 
 Your villagers have restored an 
 advanced hydroponic farm.

A New Hut!
 
 Your villagers have restored one of the 
 broken huts! Your tribe can now support a 
 larger population.

The Clothing Hut
 
 Your villagers can now spend extra tech 
 points to customize their outfits.

The Love Shack
 
 Your villagers now have a private, romantic 
 place to which they can retreat.

Fire!
 
 When a fire is burning, your villagers 
 are happier and less vulnerable to disease.

The Lake
 
 Fish! The lake is full of life once again, and 
 your villagers have a regular source of food.

The Buried Mausoleum
 
 Your villagers have restored the mausoleum, 
 and once again have a place to honor their dead.

Relic Collection
 
 Your children collected all of the 
 relics found on Isola!
 Your maximum village population 
 is increased by 5.

Lab Equipment Collection
 
 Your children collected all of the 
 science items found on 
 Isola! Your maximum village population 
 is increased by 5.

All Collections Complete!
 
 Well done! Your children completed both 
 of the collections. In addition to 
 keeping the collections, your maximum 
 village population is increased by 5!
Demo version has a max population of 9!
Only available in the full version!
Making a granary out of the fence
The heathen building master is not watching!
Something could be built from this lumber.
The heathen's challenge is not ready yet!
The heathen science master is not watching!
The chief is not home right now!

One morning, the villagers noticed that the beach looked very wrong. The waves had ceased their normal rhythm, and the water had receded so far that it almost looked as though the ocean itself was drying up. Their apprehension became alarm as a powerful tsunami crashed down upon the village, obliterating structures, and, sadly, sweeping many villagers to a watery end.

One morning, the villagers noticed that there was an aggressive and toxic mold spreading inside the food bin and ruining the contents. The frantic villagers do their best to save the food, but they can't save it all...
It's springtime, and all the flowers are in bloom. Many of the villagers suffer a temporary bout of hay fever.
Today is the day that the villagers commemorate their arrival on the island of Isola with dancing, celebration and feasts!
Today is the first day of the rainy season, marked by the first afternoon monsoon. Wow! It's really coming down!
An unseasonably cold, wet wind has blown through the village. The villagers were going to huddle around the fire, but the wet, icy drizzle put out the fire!
Army ants came and devoured the crops!
Aphids have infested the crops and rendered much of the food unusable.
Some very unusual green crystals have been found near a cave where lightning struck. The scientists can definitely use this. \n Your tribe gains tech points.

The heathens have a poor grasp of research techniques, and explosions are a common result of their haphazard methods. However, this time one of them managed to create the most truly offensive, foul, and utterly eye-watering cloud of lingering gas to ever assault a nose! This cloud has spread throughout the village, and everyone has no choice but to hide until it clears.

One day, one of the villagers responsible for a lot of the cooking finds a small bottle full of red juice. It smells like herbs, so the villager puts it into the food. Everyone is shocked by the meal, which burns their mouths! Later on, everyone seems to need to relieve themselves at the same time!
There was a big rainstorm overnight that caused the stream to overflow its banks. It made a bit of a mess, but it deposited rich, fertile silt over all the crops. It should help them grow.
One of the heathens brings a vial to show his tribesmen by the noni bush. He trips and spills the substance on the ground. A few days later, the noni bush seems to have produced a lot more fruit!

An adorable but noisy lemur has taken an interest in the lab recently. The little animal loves attention and keeps chattering and squeaking at the researchers until they play with him. He's so cute that no one wants to chase him off, even though he is keeping them from working. They resign themselves to just accommodating him until he gets bored and moves on. Your villagers lose some tech points.

Today the villagers decide to celebrate mushrooms, in all their sizes, colors and deliciousness! Such industry from those little youngsters is indeed worthy of praise and glad celebration! There will be dancing and cake for the children.

Wasps have made their way through the brambles and started to make nests around the village. Unaware of the unwelcome visitors, the villagers continue playing and working nearby. Many villagers have been stung, and some of them are experiencing a bad reaction to the stings.

Today the villagers decide to celebrate collecting their 500th mushroom. Such industry from those little youngsters is indeed worthy of praise and glad celebration! There will be dancing and cake for the children.
A large barrel full of giggling infants comes bobbing down the stream. For some reason, nobody acts particularly surprised. They are happily adopted.
A large barrel full of giggling infants comes bobbing down the stream. For some reason, these babies prefer the heathens and are adopted by them.

A freak wind has come up, filling the air with salt-laden sand, apparently from some nearby salt flat. The salty dust is stifling and burns the villagers' eyes, and they all have to hide until things settle down.
The Canoe from the Other Side
A canoe has just landed on the beach, piloted by a villager from another part of Isola.

Sitting alone one afternoon, {name} sees someone standing alone at the edge of the forest. Approaching this stranger, {he/she} is filled with warmth and euphoria. Upon reaching the edge of the forest, it turns out that the stranger was just a trick of the light, but {name} is sure it meant more than this. {name} gains faith!

One morning the villagers notice that strange footprints have appeared on the ground overnight. They later discover that a wealth of honeycombs have appeared, seemingly out of nowhere.\n \n Your village gains {award} food.

One morning the villagers notice that strange footprints have appeared on the ground overnight. They later discover that someone or something has stolen some food.\n \n Your village has lost {award} food.

One morning the villagers notice that strange footprints have appeared on the ground overnight. They later discover a number of very useful scientific instruments that seem to have come out of nowhere, as though they simply fell from the sky.\n \n Your village has gained {award} tech points.

One morning the villagers notice that strange footprints have appeared on the ground overnight. They later discover that someone or something has stolen some important research tools.\n \n Your village has lost {award} tech points.
Today is the day that the villagers pay their respects to those who have passed on.

Today is the day that the villagers give thanks to those that guide their fate and for all the blessings they enjoy on the island of Isola. There will be dancing and ceremonies, followed by a sumptuous feast!

One of the more meticulous farmers has just noticed that there are a whole bunch of berries growing way in the back, where they had been previously overlooked. It looks like there are quite a few more berries left than they thought!

The villagers hear a racket in the distance that sounds like a large drum rolling down a hill. A moment later, they see a barrel with little heads peeking out of it appear at the top of the highest waterfall. Horrified, they watch it plummet down the waterfalls until it reaches the pond where it slowly bobs about, and they manage to grab it before it sinks. Much to their relief, they find several giggling kids in the barrel, completely unharmed!

Some small children are heard giggling with glee, when to everyone's astonishment, a handful of toddlers shoot out of the bushes and splash into the hot springs! Still giggling, one of the children shouts: "Wanna do the slide again!" The villagers realize that it may take a very long time to find a way back to the children's village, because there are many treacherous features on Isola that isolate villages from one another. All they can do for now is take care of these children.
The villagers have been feeling glum and moody recently. Seeing the sacred tree in such a sorry state has had an adverse effect on their health and sense of well-being.

A respected master from another tribe has decided to join the expedition to this part of the island. {He/She} brings news that the fabled golden child from the south shore has gone missing. \n The newcomer is welcomed to the tribe.

A tame bird is found with a note tied to its leg. It bears news from another village saying that there are signs that the balance is starting to be restored to the island through the combined efforts of the other tribes. Scientific evidence follows... \n Your tribe gains some tech from the document.
The villagers have been very happy and ambitious lately. Encouraged and inspired by the improving health of the sacred tree, everyone seems to feel rejuvenated.

As the sun comes up, the tribe is greeted by desperate crying coming from the bushes. Several babies have been abandoned by someone, although they have been carefully swaddled to keep them warm and comfortable. Some of the tribe's women graciously volunteer to take care of the poor infants.
{name} woke up with lots of weird bites on {his/her} arm and thinks maybe bed bugs are infesting the huts.
Search for the bugs all night

{name} finds that {he/she} just cannot get back to sleep knowing that these biting pests are hiding somewhere in {his/her} bed. {He/She} turns the whole place inside out, fumigating with a smoldering piece of wood, until {he/she} is satisfied that it's safe to go back to sleep. Unfortunately, it is now dawn, and {he/she} is exhausted.

{name} is not happy about the bug infestation, but {he/she} is too tired to do anything about it now. {name} decides to go back to sleep. In the morning, {he/she} is covered with itchy and mildly infected bites. The tribe decides that this infestation must be dealt with and thoroughly fumigates the village with herbal smoke.
{name} Has found one of the heathen masks on the ground.

{name} puts the mask on to see how it feels to be a heathen. It is strangely comforting to be hidden behind this thing... after a while, maybe too long, it starts to feel very comfortable, and the idea of starting over seems fun. {name} decides to join the heathens in their abandon and frolicking and is a believer no more.
One day while playing, little {name} finds an unusual toy. On closer examination {he/she} is fairly certain that {he/she} saw a heathen child playing with it before.

Though it probably wasn't the right thing to do, little {name} keeps the toy and is able to glean some insight into the ways of the heathens - at least the ways of heathen children. \n {name} gains research skill.

{name} decides to return the toy to the little heathen child that {he/she} believes to be the toy's rightful owner. The child was obviously looking for the lost toy and is very happy to get it back. The two play together for a while, and {name} feels good for having made a friend and for the knowledge of having acted in accordance with the best traditions of {his/her} people. \n {name} gains devotion skill, and {his/her} faith is strengthened.
{name} decides that it might be fun to try jumping off the bridge, tethered by stretchy vines, in pursuit of a new thrill
What a ride! That was fun! {name} becomes obsessed with mastering the "stretchy-vine jump" and forgets about all of {his/her} other ambitions and obligations.
Late one night, {name} spots a mysterious figure working in the lab...

"Hello. My name is Biggles. Nice to meet you! Alas, I'm afraid you've seen too much." Biggles smiles and raises a jeweled talisman. There is a flash of light. When {name} wakes up, {he/she} can't seem to remember anything, even {his/her} own name! Oddly, {name} seems to have somehow gained uncanny insights into matters of science.

Using ordinary equipment from the lab, the man performs a number of miraculous procedures far beyond the villager's knowledge. He knows he's being watched, and, without turning around, he says, "My name is Biggles. I am here to correct certain errors. You'll thank me later!" He puts some glowing objects in his pockets and vanishes in a blinding light. He has left behind some of his amazing improvised devices. \n \n Your village gains {award} tech points.
{name} finds a way into the five pools. What a treat!

{name} is rejuvenated by the warm, bubbly water in the pools. However, {name} decides, in the interest of caution, to get out before {he/she} is noticed and to be thankful for the time in the pools, however brief.

{name} is rejuvenated by the warm, bubbly water in the pools. {He/She} realizes that it's only a matter of time before {he/she} is caught, but thinks "Who are these heathens to hog up these lovely baths?" Before long, {he/she} is indeed noticed and quickly surrounded! {name} hides {his/her} face in fear, but by the time the crowd disperses, it is a mask that hides {his/her} face, and the heathens add one more to their ranks.
{name} decides that if {he/she} cannot see this Guiding Hand, maybe it does not actually exist. {He/She} looks up and demands a sign right this minute!

Out of nowhere, hundreds of butterflies circle {name}. Already filled with doubt, however, {name} is unconvinced and believes there is a natural explanation for this phenomenon. Faith must come from within.

Faith must come from within, and a doubter will not be convinced this way. Eventually, {name} overcomes {his/her} doubt, though. {He/She} becomes one of the more outspoken believers that someone is guiding events on the island.
Little {name} becomes curious about the masked people and stakes out a secret spot from which to observe them more closely. After nearly an hour, {he/she} gets caught by a heathen!

Little {name} barely manages to get away. {He/She} did manage to figure out some things about these mysterious, masked people before {he/she} had to flee, however. Perhaps this will come in handy in the future.

The heathen, as it turns out, is not hostile, but is understandably concerned about being spied on. After a fairly lengthy conversation, they reach an understanding, and the heathen brings the child back to {his/her} parents. The grateful parents offer food items in thanks. Furthermore, little {name} feels that {he/she} has learned something about the wants and needs of the strange, masked people. Perhaps this will be handy later.
{name} notices that in the process of trying to use the lab, the heathens are trashing it. {name} would like to try to prevent some of the damage.
There are a lot of them; better not!
Just as {name} attempts to show them something, the silly heathens manage to set off an explosion right next to {him/her}
{name} manages to convince them to stop mixing acids and bases. This should reduce the frequency of lab explosions.
{name} decides that there are too many heathens to safely approach, and they don't look like they feel much like listening, anyway. {name} decides it might be best to leave them alone.

One of the villagers notices that little {name} is missing and thinks a heathen must be responsible. One of the adults confronts the heathen regarding little {name}. The heathen seems very upset and scary.

Believers come to the rescue and chase off the heathen. The believers lose their opportunity to question the heathen about little {name}, but {he/she} is found days later with the heathen child, both having caught colds from having been lost outside these last few days.
The believer and the heathen realize that their children may have gone off somewhere together. They share information about the children's favorite spots and quickly find them.

Offering a tour, the heathen is delighted to see how advanced the believers are and offers a tour in return. It is most enlightening to the believers. However, the heathen envoy, overwhelmed by the believers' wonders, succumbs to temptation and steals some minor articles from the believers.
The heathen is disappointed, but leaves in peace.

{name} has been investigating certain sites in this new part of the island and believes that one of these sites may have been an important center of the original inhabitants' civilization. Today, {he/she} has found some amazing artifacts to support {his/her} theory.

{name} prepares a presentation based on {his/her} independent research. The findings are well received by the believers at large. Many believe that these findings will lead to whole new avenues of research. \n Your tribe gains a level in science.

Unfortunately, the research is not well received. The villagers do not believe that the objects are genuine, nor do they believe that this field of endeavor is likely to lead to any practical results. {name} is very disappointed and decides that {he/she} may not be cut out to be a scientist after all.

{name} decides that {he/she} will need the help of the other researchers to properly conduct {his/her} investigation into these mysterious objects. The research is difficult, but gradually the objects begin to give up their ancient secrets.

{name} has discovered that the heathens have some important scrolls in their dirty hovels. They don't seem to realize what they have, but {name} knows that these scrolls could be very helpful to their own research. {name} believes that {he/she} could either try to negotiate a trade or perhaps {he/she} could steal them, with the proper distraction.
Trade some food for the scrolls

{name} teaches the heathens a recipe well known to {his/her} tribe for producing foul-smelling smoke clouds, but convinces the heathens that it's a cure for baldness. When the smoke clouds erupt, {name} sneaks in and steals the scrolls. Of course, {name} will not be trusted by the heathens again, as not a one of them grew back any hair! Later, {name} discovers that there is a piece missing, and now {he/she} is in no position to negotiate for it. \n Your tribe gains 1500 tech points

{name} arranges a barter session with an envoy from the heathen camp. Finally, they agree to trade the scrolls for 100 food. The trade goes smoothly, and {name} gains some respect from the heathens for his honest business practices. Also, one of the heathens produces a piece that was missing from the scrolls that was apparently stuck to his foot! Good thing they mentioned it! \n Your tribe gains 3000 tech points.

Fruit bats have come to inhabit the nearby trees as a stop in their migration. They could either be scared away, to prevent them from eating up the fruit, or observed to see if anything can be learned from them.

{name} decides to just sit and quietly observe the bats. After a while {he/she} realizes that plants and grasses are growing quite rapidly under the trees where they roost. Their droppings must be an excellent fertilizer. {name} realizes that this could be the key to raising sustainable crops! Unfortunately the bats have devoured all of the noni fruit in the process. \n Your tribe gains a level of farming tech.
{name} has little patience for freeloading bats, who are devouring their fruit! {He/She} gathers the tribe to drive them off!
The Aphids in the Noni Bush
Small juice-sucking bugs are literally sucking the life out of the crops! Something must be done, but this must be handled wisely, because they could become a chronic problem.

After some study, the villagers figure out that there are small creatures that live in certain types of soil that will eat the aphid's eggs before they hatch. This process is not immediate, but it's effective and long lasting. \n {name} gains farming expertise. \n Your village gains tech points.
The villagers decide to try using a potion to destroy the pests outright. While it is completely and immediately effective, it also destroys most of the noni fruit!

One of the heathens sees that the new arrivals seem to really know what they are doing and asks to join the newcomers. {He/She} seems very sincere, but some of the villagers are a little suspicious, because this petitioner can't have come to understand much about the believers' ways or culture in such a short time. Should they welcome the heathen into their tribe or politely send {him/her} back to {his/her} people?
The villagers' trust is well-founded. It turns out that {name} is exactly as {he/she} has represented {himself/herself}, and the tribe now has a new member!

Alas, as it turns out, {name} was indeed a spy and has sabotaged the research area. (Heathens seem to possess a singular talent for ruining the lab, so this is not much of a surprise.) \n Your tribe loses 2000 tech points.

The villagers politely explain that this is a big decision, and {name} should probably take some time to understand the culture of the believers before so profoundly changing the course of {his/her} life. "The door will still be open for you later if you still want to join us later." they tell {him/her}. {name} seems to understand the wisdom of this advice and returns to {his/her} people in peace.
{name} has found a strange thing woven of reeds. {He/She} thinks it could be either a hat or some kind of strainer to boil grains in.
Use it as a cooking strainer

The thing works splendidly as a strainer for their traditional method of preparing wild grains. Unfortunately, it doesn't last long, because it was, in fact, a straw hat and never meant for this purpose. So, it turns out to be a short-term boon, but a boon nonetheless.
One day, {name} finds a very unusual blossom on a strange plant that no one has ever seen in bloom before. At the bottom of the cup-like blossom is an irresistibly sweet smelling nectar.
{name} takes a sip of the nectar and quickly feels rejuvenated! Moreover {he/she} feels incredibly energetic! Has everyone else just slowed down?

It's better to not mess with consuming random things without thorough research. The sample is brought back to the other researchers for further study, which yields encouraging results. \n Your tribe gains 2000 tech points.

One of the heathens has a sack on their head instead of their mask and seems very upset. On a nearby rock lies a wooden mask broken in two. {name} knows that a simple glue can easily be made from noni sap and sand, but the heathens clearly don't know how to make it. On the other hand, {name} could fix it poorly to trick the heathen into giving up the mask! \n How should {name} help the heathen?

{name} begins to fix the broken mask, but before {he/she} can make the heathen understand {his/her} intentions, the heathen goes wild and injures {him/her}. Ultimately the heathen realizes {name}'s intentions and becomes quite grateful! Though slightly injured, {name} appears to have made a friend and gained valuable experience in dealing with the heathens.

The heathen is outraged by the feeble attempt at manipulation on {name}'s part. The heathen puts the sack back on and calls the other heathens. They quickly overwhelm and capture {name}, forcing {him/her} to wear a mask.
Little {name} has discovered a vial filled with a weird liquid that smells strongly of some combination of cheese and peppermint.

{name} swallows the strange liquid, gagging as it goes down. "I probably should not have drunk that" {he/she} thinks to {himself/herself}. A few hours later, {name} starts noticing all the subtle aromas of the world that {he/she} never really noticed before. {He/She} can even smell mushrooms from far away. {name} really loves mushrooms and begins putting {his/her} newly extra-sensitive nose to work finding every last mushroom hidden in this part of the island. Unfortunately, as a side effect, {name} is overly sensitive to strong odors and, therefore, has trouble with any kind of work other than farming. \n Your tribe gains food.
{name} has heard about strange, magical vials, and this one smells terrible. {He/She} would have to be crazy to drink this one!
{name} found a vial with an irresistible, floral-smelling liquid inside.
You shouldn't drink strange liquids. You might shrink or turn into a baby or something!

One day, {name } steps on something that hurts {his/her} foot. What can this be? It's invisible! By feeling it, {name} figures out that it's a small vial and believes that this one, being invisible, must contain a potion of great power. For days, {he/she} agonizes over the decision of whether or not to sample its mysterious contents.

{name} finally decides to drink the contents and is surprised that it only contains a tiny sip of berry juice. Also, quite surprisingly, it refills itself, this time with honey water. {name} puzzles over this for a time and finally realizes that the vial is a lesson: Don't be afraid of the unknown, because having the courage to discover often yields a sweet surprise! {name} takes this lesson to heart and becomes curious about the true nature of all things.
{name} does not think it is worth the risk. Any possible benefit would never make up for all the pain and trouble of ingesting a potentially toxic substance. Better just forget it.

{name} believes that the fruit would cook faster in the cooking pit if {he/she} was balanced on top of the covered fruit, applying constant pressure while it cooks. This is obviously extremely dangerous, but could it work?

{name} sets the fruit under a banana leaf and begins to balance on the hard round bump. In a few moments the fruit begins to soften, and {name} quickly hops off and retrieves the cooked fruit! It is very effective and {name} is setting the bar among farmers!

{name} sets the fruit under a banana leaf and prepares to step onto the fruit. Even before {his/her} foot reaches the covered fruit, {he/she} slips and stumbles into the hot coals! That was a bad idea...
{name} knows better than to try this kind of crazy thing. Those coals are hot and very unforgiving.

One evening, {name} encounters a mysterious stranger. Ordinarily, {name} would just run away, but there is something familiar about this stranger... something from the stories of the older parts of the island. The stranger instructs {name} to gather the other children for an important lesson.
Run away and tell the adults

{name} decides that this is a matter that must be handled by the adults. {He/She} runs home and wakes the adults, who immediately form a search party to find the mysterious and creepy intruder. However, by the time they arrive, he is gone. All that remains is a strange cloud of luminous smoke.

The mysterious stranger gazes across his audience and announces, "Fear not! It is only me, Biggles! Perhaps you have heard of me? Yes? No? I have an important lesson for you clever children. You know, sometimes when people make a mistake, and they admit their mistake, they may learn from it, but those who fail to see their error are doomed to repeat it. You know, there are others on this island.Others who you have not yet met. Others who, for a very long time, have denied their past mistakes. They believe that only the way of magic is important and ignore the balance that is nature.They have grand designs and must not succeed. But there is still time! Be ever watchful my children! Be ever watchful!" With these words the man vanishes leaving only a cloud of luminous smoke.

{name} hears crying and finds a village child stuck high up on a branch in the great Tree of Life. No amount of coaxing will bring {him/her} down. It will be very dangerous for an adult to climb that high on the tree and help the child down. Perhaps the child should be left to have a lesson about consequences.

{name} climbs up the tree and helps the child find a path back down through the branches. Predictably, {name}'s own descent does not go so smoothly. The second branch {he/she} touches snaps loudly! {name} tumbles down through the branches and hit the ground hard. Oh well. Parenting requires sacrifices.

Children have to learn about the consequences of their actions. {name} leaves the child. Hours later the small, subdued youth returns to the village, bruised and angry. It is not obvious whether it was a lesson about consequences or just a lesson about falling down.

Two children have been constantly fighting over a pretty, round shell.{name} is sick of the bickering and decides to intervene. The children will have to either be taught to share the shell, or they will have to decide who will keep it.
Sharing is important and teaching children about this is good parenting. They agree to share the shell, and {name} reflects on how well this went.

Not everything can be shared, and in this case a lesson about negotiation is more valuable. However, even after they pick an owner for the shell, one of the children feels very bad, outmatched at the debate over the shell. Still, the fighting has stopped. {name}'s approach was innovative and effective, although maybe a bit harsh.

{name} discovers a mysterious figure lurking by the tree one night. Sensing {name}, the figure turns, smiles and says: "Hello, my child. My name is Biggles. Perhaps you have heard of me? I have been watching you. Your people have done well in returning the balance to Isola. I will tell you something: The island, like life, is a wheel. This tree you see here is its axle. To restore balance the axle must be true. Now, because your people are worthy, I will answer one question:"
How should we care for our people?
How should we care for the tree?

"Yes, I see that you are a good and caring people. I will teach you a secret." Biggles teaches {name} some advanced and arcane medical knowledge When {name} turns to thank him, he is simply not there! Where could he have gone?

"Yes, I see that you are a good and wise people. I will teach you a secret." Biggles teaches {name} some advanced and arcane techniques in dendrology. When {name} turns to thank him, he is simply not there! Where could he have gone?
